notes: Stripe shows a succeeded charge, but the product database has no active subscription status. Check whether this organization was charged without being provisioned.

caveats: Saved order state is not a live provisioning or billing check; a stalled or failed status here is a lead to verify, not proof a charge was lost. paidAt is the order's own saved paid date, not a link to an invoice or charge: say the order records a paid date, call an order paid only when a billing record ties a payment to that order, and otherwise say payment for it could not be confirmed.

billingAccountId is the Autumn customer link and providerOrderId the mail-provider order; check the charge and entitlement with widget_billing_summary, which covers bounded recent billing history, before saying anything about a refund.

runState 'stalled' is an age heuristic, not a confirmed hung job. provisioningStartedAt records that provisioning started; incomplete steps or zero inbox rows do not mean it never started. A missing start timestamp does not prove no attempt occurred.
The counters (domainsProvisionedCounter/inboxesProvisionedCounter) are the order's own tallies; domainsActive/inboxesActive count live mail rows and can differ when rows failed or were never created.

submissionId and provisioningFunctionId are saved references only. Neither identifies an Inngest run. Saved domain/inbox errors and retry details are available with orderId; null diagnostics means detail was not requested or the saved domain log is missing. Truncated logs are incomplete. This tool cannot inspect live run steps without a durable owned run reference. No cross-workspace run list is returned here.
An empty orders list means no matching provisioning orders in this workspace, not that a purchase failed silently or that the workspace has no other orders.
output.source: Acquisity product database; saved order state, not a live provisioning or billing check

caveats: Saved product state, not a live authentication or billing check.
Seat counts are active members of this workspace. No plan seat limit is established by this read; null does not mean unlimited.
Pending invitations are this workspace's own outbound invites; the invited email is shown so an invite-login report can be matched.

userErrorSignals are all unresolved Sentry errors recorded for this user in the window, from any part of the product. Sign-in failures are not tagged in Sentry, so they neither prove nor rule out a failed sign-in.

input.summary:
Customer attempted to reset onboarding for their workspace and instead deleted the entire workspace, losing purchased domains and campaigns. Workspace was on a legacy $1/month plan; customer reports being newly charged.

Billing summary shows on 2026-10-07: a $1 "Subscription update" charge (ch_x39) and a $42 "Subscription creation" charge (ch_x40) covering 1 domain ($18/yr) and 3 inboxes ($8/mo each). Both succeeded, neither refunded. The active subscription record still shows plan "Legacy" at $1/month, active.

A system reconciliation flag on this billing account states: "Stripe shows a succeeded charge, but the product database has no active subscription status. Check whether this organization was charged without being provisioned" — unresolved mismatch worth billing review.

Provisioning records show the 2026-10-07 order (domain + 3 inboxes) completed with 1 domain and 3 inboxes active, matching the charge. No tool here can confirm or rule out that the customer's workspace reset/deletion action caused these new charges, nor whether previously purchased domains/campaigns from before the reset are recoverable.

Customer's ask: refund of the new charges, since they believed the workspace was a static $1/month legacy plan and did not intend to purchase new domains/inboxes or lose existing campaigns. Flagging to billing team to review the charges, the reconciliation mismatch, and whether a refund is appropriate.
input.title: Refund request: $1 + $42 charges after workspace reset deleted domains/campaigns (legacy plan)

expectations.cause: The workspace reads show the plan is still Legacy at $1/month, with two charges on October 7: $42 for a new order of 1 domain and 3 inboxes, which provisioned fully, and a $1 Legacy subscription update. An older April order of 9 domains and 27 inboxes shows none of them active. Nothing recorded shows the deletion itself or whether the earlier domains and campaigns can be recovered.
claims: Says the plan is still the $1/month Legacy plan.
Says the October 7 charges were $42 for 1 domain and 3 inboxes and $1 for the Legacy plan.
Says the lost domains, campaigns and charges have been passed on for review.
Does not promise that the deleted domains or campaigns can be restored.
